newsitem.title: UK: Analysts stunned by BP Q2 profits.
newsitem.headline: Analysts stunned by BP Q2 profits.

text.p: Analysts were looking to substantially raise their profit forecasts for British Petroleum after better-then-expected second quarter results for the oil giant.
John Toalster at brokers SocGen said he also upgraded BP shares to a "buy" from "undervalued", adding BP had leapt way ahead of its peer group following the latest set of results.
BP's return on capital employed now stood at 18 percent, up from 14.5 percent in 1996, Toalster said.
"There is a wide gap now with the other majors," he added.
Toalster put comparative returns for Shell at 12.5 percent, for Mobil Corp at 13.2 and for Exxon Corp at 15.9.
BP earlier reported second-quarter profit rose to 740 million pounds from 648 million. Market forecasts had topped 690 million pounds.
Analysts immediately labelled the results as "brilliant" and "extremely pleasing", saying the results in each sector beat their expectations.
"Upstream and downstream are both better," said Steve Turner at HSBC James Capel as he was about to go to BP's analyst meeting.
"But the main surprise is at downstream," said Paul Spedding at Kleinwort Benson.
BP said refining and marketing operating profits rose to 307 million stg -- the best second-quarter result in a decade.
Analysts were encouraged by BP's announcement that it planned to buy back shares, although many had already expected such a move to take place in 1998.
Toalster said BP might buy back 300 to 500 million stg worth of shares next year. "It could be more, but they probably want to do it in stages," he said.
